Audit: QCEPC36G (Collings et al. 2026, ESSA position statement on ACL injury risk)
Checked against QCEPC36G.pages.txt (23 pages; pp. 16-23 are mostly references) and QCEPC36G.prepare.json.

Verified unchanged
- Frontmatter matches Zotero: item QCEPC36G, attachment 5JGMN8JU, version 7117, DOI 10.1007/s40279-026-02450-3 (printed p. 1), status ingested, usable, page.
- Table 1 figures (64%, 7/2,479 vs 14/2,085; 76%, 3/675 vs 16/850; 82%; 87%; KLIP +114%; Balance +277%; ages 13-26) match p. 4. The count of 10 reductions / 2 increases / 4 significant is correct.
- 60% meta-analytic estimate (pp. 1, 3), 3-8x female risk (p. 2), adherence 66 +/- 21% from 19 studies (p. 6), <50 ms rupture (p. 8), 5-10 degree markerless accuracy (p. 9) all match.
- Existing reporting flags are correct: PEP [22] 70% in text vs 41% in Table 1, FIFA 11 [23] 29% vs 20% (pp. 4-5); warm-up 10-30 min (pp. 1, 6) vs 15-20 min (p. 14) vs "20 min or more" (Table 4, p. 14).
- The brief makes clear the findings are a synthesis of other studies, not new pooling.

Changes made
1. Population, return-to-play context: "Post-reconstruction athletes are mentioned as a separate high-risk group [p. 1, p. 12]". p. 12 does not say this. Now: prior ACL injury/reconstruction discussed for high re-injury rates and as candidates for targeted work [p. 1, p. 9, p. 15].
2. Inclusion criteria for risk-factor studies: "at least one significant univariable intrinsic risk factor" merged an inclusion rule with the extraction rule. Now matches p. 3: one or more intrinsic risk factors with a univariable analysis, at least five ACL injuries, and only significant factors extracted.
3. PEDro: removed "because the authors did not rate the studies themselves" (not printed). Now: extracted from nine previous systematic reviews, collated by median [p. 2-3] (sentence runs across the page break).
4. Risk factors: "prior ACL injury (strongest)" overstated the text. Now "the most consistently identified" (p. 9).
5. Non-significant trials: the brief said the authors attribute non-significance in "several other" studies to small injury numbers. The text says this only for PEP [22] and FIFA 11 [23] (p. 5). Narrowed.
6. Limitations, biomechanical proxy measures: locator was p. 13; the statement is in Future Research on p. 15 (and Table 5, p. 16). Fixed.
7. Practitioner interpretation: "Physical screening should not be used to pick who gets targeted work" was stronger than the authors. Now: screening cut-offs should not decide; Tier 2 is at practitioner discretion, not pre-determined rules (p. 15); the authors still allow testing for deficits, with unclear benefit from correcting them (p. 12). Still labelled as interpretation.

Residual concerns for Eric
- The intervention inclusion rule differs between text and table: text excludes "fewer than 5 ACL injuries" (p. 2), Table 1 footnote says "more than a total of five" (p. 4). HarmoKnee (0 + 5 = 5 injuries) meets the first but not the second. Not added to the brief.
- The 60% figure is cited from other meta-analyses (refs 19, 20), not computed here; the underlying studies are mostly small and at high risk of bias by the authors' own account (p. 6).
- This is a narrative position statement with a one-author search and screening (p. 2); treat recommendations as expert synthesis, not a systematic review result.
- Two authors declare funding to build injury prevention programs (p. 16). Not mentioned in the brief.

content.text:
- **HZJ676Z9:** 2 changes. The paper never says its p-values are one-tailed, but they are. Recomputing from the printed t-statistics matches all eight exactly. So the "near-significant" strength-coach results (p = 0.063 and 0.089) are about 0.13 and 0.18 two-tailed. They also run in the opposite direction to the hypothesis: worse-ranked strength staffs had slightly fewer injuries. I added both points to the brief, marked as the brief's own reading.
- **WAD5YYM2:** 6 changes. The DOI isn't printed anywhere in the paper, so I emptied the frontmatter `doi`. I also removed a design claim the text doesn't support ("one set of tests per athlete"), corrected the impulse vs peak-power claim (r = 0.38 is not significant), rewrote the scaling limitation, and made the authors' practical advice match p. 9. Main concern: the abstract presents r = 0.38 as p ≤ 0.05 and gives effect sizes that disagree with Table 7. Also, the strong and weak groups were split on relative peak force, so their large difference on it is built into the split, not a result.
- **QCEPC36G:** 7 changes. I fixed locators (one wrong page, one with no support) and two inclusion-criteria and PEDro statements that went beyond the text. I toned down "strongest" risk factor and narrowed the "small injury numbers" excuse to the two trials the authors actually name. I also toned down the screening advice in the interpretation section. Main concern: the headline 60% reduction comes from other meta-analyses of mostly small, high-bias studies. One author ran the search and screening alone. The text and Table 1 also state the inclusion rule differently (at least 5 injuries vs more than 5), which affects two studies.

Each audit file lists every change with its page and the remaining concerns. The files are in `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-kristinarash-DEV/68215dd7-b944-4535-98be-9b3a3defa4ae/scratchpad/brief/`:
